acceptance_criteria.measure: Distinct values observed for the initial TCP sequence number across 1000 connection establishments, requiring no value repetition within the set
Distinct entropy seeds observed across 1000 power cycles
Inventory entries whose version is either evidenced by a named source or explicitly null with a stated reason
Maximum elapsed time between successive checks of the inventory against the authoritative advisory source
Advisory matches for which a determination is recorded, including determinations of 'no applicable advisory found'
Inventory entries carrying a guessed or inferred version with no evidence

asil_justification.reason: This requirement is classified 'security' and it governs entropy strength and component vulnerability handling. ISO 26262 does not allocate an ASIL to a security requirement, so not_applicable is the schema's own enumerated value for that case. The trace to the safety-case skeleton records that an ungoverned component set and an unsound entropy source are both open items a safety argument must eventually account for. Recording them as open items is not the same as allocating an ASIL to them, and this field does not claim either item is closed.
asil_justification.scope_of_this_classification: This field records why safety_allocation.asil is not_applicable on this requirement. It is a statement about this record's own allocation bookkeeping inside a fictional reference project. It is not a determination about the real foxBMS 2 product and not evidence about the state of any real component set or entropy source.
what_this_does_not_assert: It does not assert conformity with ISO 26262, and it is not a certification, a type approval, or evidence of one. Nothing in this field was audited to produce it.

It does not assert human approval. human_approval_status on this record is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false, and no functional-safety expert has confirmed any of it.
It does not establish that any ASIL was correctly assigned to any safety requirement in this corpus. It explains only why this requirement is not itself an ASIL-allocated item.
It does not assert tool qualification. No tool used anywhere in this corpus has been qualified for a safety purpose.
It does not assert an ASPICE capability level for anything.

fault_reaction.allocation_basis: NO ELEMENT ALLOCATES A FAULT REACTION FOR THE SECURITY CHAIN. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.safety_strategies.fault_reaction lists four reactions and allocates them to AR-002, AR-004, AR-005 and AR-006; FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.fault_reaction lists the same four. None of them is a reaction to a detected security attack, and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.safety_strategies.fault_detection lists five detection mechanisms, none of which is a communication-integrity or authentication check. The security chain therefore has no element-level reaction budget anywhere in this corpus. That is a real gap and it is recorded as one rather than closed by inventing an allocation. The reaction this field states is the one this requirement's own statement mandates and the one its own acceptance criteria decide; who carries it technically, and within what time, is not derivable from any record that exists.
fault_reaction.budget_absence_note: No reaction_time_budget_ms is stated, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. The safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001.timing_budget.allocation has ten entries, none of which is a cybersecurity leg, and neither safety concept allocates one to the security chain, so there is no interval in this corpus against which a security reaction time could be checked. The decidable bounds that DO exist are stated in reaction_time_bound, transcribed from this record's own acceptance criteria. Inventing a millisecond figure here would create a number with nothing to verify it against, which is the failure mode finding FB2-REV-FND-000025 was raised about.
fault_reaction.derivation: Transcribed, not invented. reaction, triggered_by, diagnosis, reaction_time_bound and mode_dependence are each quoted or paraphrased from text this record already carried at revision 3: its own statement, its own acceptance_criteria and its own conditions_modes. The numeric bound in reaction_time_bound is a threshold this record's own acceptance criteria already stated; where the record states no such bound, this field says so rather than supplying one. No acceptance criterion, ASIL value, verification approach, verification_status, statement or rationale was altered by adding this field.
fault_reaction.diagnosis: Adjudication record completeness, at 100 percent of matches, including determinations of 'no applicable advisory found'. Transcribed from this record's own acceptance criteria 'Adjudication record completeness / Advisory matches for which a determination is recorded, including determinations of no applicable advisory found / 100 / % of matches' and 'Component version evidence completeness / ... / 100 / % of entries'. A match with no recorded determination is the diagnosability failure this requirement makes decidable; the record that it exists is the diagnosis.
fault_reaction.mode_dependence: Mode-independent in the sense that the record states no mode dependence, and the reason is worth stating rather than leaving as a silence: the entropy requirement applies at every boot, including the commissioning and bootloader boots, and a build-time-fixed seed is a defect in all of this record's conditions_modes (NORMAL, CHARGING, DISCHARGE, PRECHARGE, DEGRADED, COMMISSIONING) rather than only in the production ones. The component-inventory half is not a runtime mode question at all - it is a process obligation that holds between boots.
fault_reaction.open_limits: real_source_control_status on this record is 'partially_present', and the record's own block names what that means: the observed source derives an initial sequence number from a single 32-bit state seeded with a build-time literal, and an ungoverned component set is an open item. So the failure this reaction addresses is one the corpus has actually observed in the real source, which makes the absence of a verification leg more consequential, not less: verification_approach on this record is the single word 'analysis' and verification_status is not_verified, so there is no analysis in this corpus that shows the entropy source the reaction assumes exists. The reaction has no element-level allocation in either safety concept and no reaction-time budget, because FB2-SAF-SGO-000001.timing_budget has no cybersecurity leg. The named owner the statement requires for the inventory is not named in any record in this corpus, so the procedural half of this reaction has no addressable owner and cannot be audited for accountability.
fault_reaction.reaction: Two reactions, one technical and one procedural, and both are the requirement's own text. The technical half: derive the initial TCP sequence number and every other network security parameter from a cryptographically strong entropy source that is 're-seeded at every boot from a source not fixed at build time' - the failure mode being a sequence space an attacker can predict, and the reaction being that the parameter is not derived from a build-time literal at all. The procedural half: the component inventory is checked against an authoritative advisory source on a schedule and every match is adjudicated with a recorded determination, so an ungoverned or vulnerable component is a recorded, owned process outcome rather than an undetected condition.
fault_reaction.reaction_time_bound: 'Advisory monitoring interval / Maximum elapsed time between successive checks of the inventory against the authoritative advisory source / 30 days'. Transcribed from this record's own acceptance criterion. It bounds the periodicity of the procedural reaction and not any technical reaction time. No criterion in this record bounds how quickly a boot-time entropy failure is detected or acted on, and none is invented here.
fault_reaction.triggered_by: A boot at which the entropy source is not re-seeded, or is re-seeded from a value fixed at build time; an inventory entry whose version is neither evidenced by a named source nor explicitly null with a stated reason; an advisory match against the inventory with no determination recorded; or an interval longer than the scheduled one since the last advisory check.
fault_reaction.unverified_leg_note: The verification leg is absent in the real source and the record says so: real_source_control_status is 'partially_present'. This block therefore describes what the requirement specifies, not what the foxBMS 2 product does. No measurement, no timing analysis and no injection campaign exists in this corpus for any part of it.

record_verbatim.rationale: The two clauses address the two ways in which the item's security posture degrades without a code defect. The first: the real source derives the TCP initial sequence number from a single 32-bit state seeded with a build-time literal and advanced by a fixed multiplier plus a tick count, and the source itself annotates the generator as insufficient. A predictable initial sequence number removes a defence-in-depth layer of the TCP connection, so the entropy source must be sound before any authenticated protocol is layered on top of it. The second: an inventory that is never checked against an advisory source records what is present but says nothing about whether it is affected, and an inventory whose version evidence is guessed is worse than no inventory because it cannot be acted on (TARA threats THR-004, THR-008; TARA mitigations MIT-006, MIT-009).
record_verbatim.real_source_control_status_note: Part of the capability this requirement specifies is present in the real foxBMS 2 source and part is not; see real_source_presence for the itemised split.
record_verbatim.real_source_presence: Entropy control ABSENT, stated from the source. src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:79 defines ETH_SEED as the literal 53393467 and :315 seeds the generator with it; ulApplicationGetNextSequenceNumber at :344-364 and xApplicationGetRandomNumber at :395-400 both return UTIL_GetPseudoRandomNumber(), which is implemented in src/app/driver/foxmath/utils.c:109-115 as a fixed multiplier update of that single state, perturbed only by the tick count, under the in-source comment at :112 'Currently only fixed operations. Needs further improvement.'. Anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000059, FB2-SRC-COD-000072. BOUND ON CLAIM: no attack was attempted, no exploit was developed and no exploitability is asserted; the FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP receive path was not audited, so whether a predictable initial sequence number is sufficient to mount a blind attack against this stack is UNKNOWN. Component inventory: PARTIALLY PRESENT — the inventory now exists in this corpus as docs/artifacts/sources/sbom.json, with per-entry version evidence and explicit null-version reasons; the monitoring process and its owner do NOT exist. That SBOM deliberately records no vulnerability status for any component, because no advisory source was consulted and inventing a status would be a fabrication. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000073, FB2-SRC-COD-000074, FB2-SRC-COD-000077.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Corrected safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref from 'FB2-SAF-SCO-000001' to 'FB2-SAF-SCS-000001'. The previous value matched no artifact in either profile. This requirement's own mitigation prose already names the safety-case skeleton as the thing it is traced to, and the corpus's safety-case skeleton carries id FB2-SAF-SCS-000001, so the mistyped value sits one character from the intended one. The defect was a hand-entry typo inside a free-string payload field, which is why the link validator never saw it; remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000023. No acceptance criterion, ASIL value, verification approach or statement was changed. The same mistyped value also appeared in FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 threat THR-008 and was corrected in the same pass; the corpus-wide sweep finding a second instance is the evidence that this was a typing fault rather than one stale value.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the fault_reaction block that the safety-requirement completeness validator (MUT-008, safety_requirement_completeness_checker) requires and did not find. That rule used to carry an id filter '-FSR-' in id which made it structurally incapable of reporting this record, while its sibling verification_traceability_checker selected the same population - requirement plus engineering_domain equals safety - with no id filter at all. The filter has been removed from the rule, which widened its scope and weakened nothing; see finding FB2-REV-FND-000039. The block authored here is transcribed from this record's own statement, acceptance_criteria and conditions_modes, and records three absences honestly rather than filling them: neither safety concept allocates a fault reaction to any element for the security chain (element_owns_reaction is therefore false), the safety goal's timing budget has no cybersecurity leg so no reaction-time budget is stated, and the control's real-source status and unverified verification leg are carried through. No acceptance criterion, ASIL value, statement, rationale, verification approach or verification status was changed. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human has approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Defence-in-depth and process mitigation. asil is recorded as not_applicable because this is a security requirement; it is traced to the project's safety-case skeleton because an ungoverned component set and an unsound entropy source are both open items a safety argument must eventually account for, not because an ASIL is allocated to them.

standards_mappings.rationale: Named for traceability of intent only. No ISO/SAE 21434 work product exists in this corpus, no cryptography concept has been written, and no conformance is claimed. Note that the component-assessment clause is referenced as a process expectation, not as a claim that any assessment was performed.
No cybersecurity claim support process and no risk-assessment method exist in this corpus. This requirement proposes the closure and is unverified.
Referenced because component management and dependency resolution appear in the project's process inventory; no ASPICE assessment of any process has been performed or is claimed.
standards_mappings.reference: SUP.8, SUP.9, SUP.10 (supplier and third-party component management)

record_verbatim.statement: The BMS master software shall derive the initial TCP sequence number and any other network security parameter from a cryptographically strong entropy source that is re-seeded at every boot from a source not fixed at build time; and the project shall maintain, under a named owner, an inventory of every third-party component in the target and in the commissioning toolchain, each entry carrying the evidence for its version, together with a scheduled process that checks that inventory against an authoritative advisory source and records the result.
record_verbatim.title: SEC-000005: Cryptographically strong entropy for network security parameters, and governed third-party component management

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-SAF-SEC-000005` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
